clue.text: Fruitful source of information

parts.note: the plant that literally bears fruit doubles as the informal channel through which rumours and news spread

explanation.surface: A productive place to pick up facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitful' reads as 'productive', but here it is literal: the plant bears grapes, and the same word names the rumour mill ('I heard it on the ...').
explanation.definitionFit: The rumour network of gossip passed person to person is named after the climbing fruit plant.

clue.text: Peer has agitated for reform

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the two words before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman is stirred up in favour of political reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a member of the House of Lords; it is just fodder, with 'has', for the anagram signalled by 'agitated'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something can mean to give it a new form, to remould it.

clue.text: Philosopher attached to a body of soldiers

parts.note: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher
on means attached to, as in a button on a coat

explanation.surface: A thinker has joined up with an army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small military unit, a subdivision of a company, is a troop of soldiers.

clue.text: Give legal force to girl with new idea accepting model

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the rearranged word holds the next piece
new tells you to make the word idea afresh, rearranging its letters

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A woman with a fresh notion takes on a model to make it lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns IDEA into IDAE, and 'accepting' puts T inside it after the A: IDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify or make legally binding is to confirm officially.

clue.text: Slip by the continental church feature

parts.note: el is 'the' in Spanish, a continental language
an apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer on the Continent lets a detail pass unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: When time slips by it passes away.

clue.text: Declaration will reveal nothing

parts.note: to manifest is to show or reveal
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A statement that, in the end, discloses nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's published statement of policy is a public pronouncement of aims.

clue.text: It is fallacious about to be in eluded with all the members of a profession

definitions.text: all the members of a profession

indicators.note: to be included says the piece before is to go inside the word for fallacious

parts.note: faulty means flawed or fallacious, as in faulty reasoning
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Something false is on the point of being let into a whole profession.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'in eluded' is an OCR slip for 'included'. 'to be included' puts C (circa) inside FAULTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of lawyers or doctors is called the faculty, as in the medical faculty.

clue.text: Gazing about

explanation.surface: Someone staring around.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarding means looking at, gazing upon; it also means concerning, on the subject of.

clue.text: Unauthorised divulgation of water escaping

explanation.surface: A secret disclosure described as spilt water.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is both an unofficial release of secret information and fluid seeping out through a hole.

clue.text: Dolt and lieutenant accept gold in the attack

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the two pieces before it hold the next one between them

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dolt
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A fool and an officer take a share of gold during the raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' splits the dolt and the officer apart so the gold sits between them; 'in the' is just linking.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent onslaught, a direct strike against someone.

clue.text: Flower stiffly formal and acceptable with the French

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper or formal
U means upper-class and therefore socially acceptable
la is 'the' in French (feminine)

explanation.surface: A bloom described as starchy but agreeable, with a French touch.
explanation.walkthrough: U for acceptable comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' labels for upper-class and middle-class British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of plants including the primrose and cowslip.

clue.text: May has lots of cuddles

parts.note: may and can both express permission
oodles means lots, a great quantity

explanation.surface: A woman called May gets plenty of hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' poses as a name or the month; it is the verb 'may', giving CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously.

clue.text: Important time certain for removal

parts.note: an era is a significant period of history
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A key moment is certain to bring about a clear-out.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the wiping out or deletion of something.

clue.text: Showed indignation having been despatched in a rush

indicators.note: in puts the despatched word inside the plant word

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
sent means despatched

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed at being sent off in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' looks like haste but is the waterside plant; 'in' holds the despatched word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resented something is to have felt bitter about it.

clue.text: Apple used for curdling milk

explanation.surface: A fruit used in cheese-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is an old variety of dessert apple (the reinette) and the enzyme preparation that sets milk for cheese.

clue.text: Hurried, fired and searched thoroughly

parts.note: ran means hurried
sacked means fired from a job

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off, lost their job, and was then searched.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to go through it hunting, often roughly, for something.

clue.text: Mayfly left existing only for a day

parts.note: Ephemera is the scientific genus of the mayfly

explanation.surface: A mayfly departs, having lived for just a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The mayfly's adult life famously lasts about a day, which is where the genus name comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Something short-lived, from Greek for 'lasting a day', is fleeting.

clue.text: Last to refuse to give up

explanation.surface: The final one to refuse surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue or endure, and to keep going obstinately despite opposition.

clue.text: Case of the blackleg and poet

parts.note: a scab is a strike-breaker, also called a blackleg
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A lawsuit involving a strike-breaker and a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' poses as a legal case; it is a sheath. A blackleg is British slang for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath for a sword or dagger.

clue.text: It is hard to get rain all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: It is difficult to get rain to fall everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The igneous rock is proverbially tough and durable.

clue.text: Making do with a stone

explanation.surface: Managing with only a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping means managing in difficulty; a coping stone is a top stone on a wall.

clue.text: Flexible record returned as it jumped about

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the record's letters are read backwards

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: jumped means moved about suddenly, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A bendy record came back and leapt about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LP into PL; 'jumped' turns AS IT into ASTI; then C for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mouldable can be bent or shaped easily.

clue.text: Ornament allowed after hug

indicators.note: after puts the permitted word behind the cuddle word

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery permitted after an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is a decorative band or small necklace worn around the throat.

clue.text: Wizard concocts errors about this in France

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
concocts means makes up or mixes, so the letters of errors are rearranged

parts.note: ce is French for 'this'

explanation.surface: A magician cooks up mistakes concerning something in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocts' makes SORRER, which 'about' wraps round the French word for 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a magician who practises witchcraft.

clue.text: One's total possessions, a broken tea-set

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of the tea-set are reassembled

explanation.surface: All someone owns is a smashed tea service.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything a person owns, especially at death, is their property and assets.

clue.text: Image of doctor left in a spirited meeting

indicators.note: in puts the doctor and left inside the meeting

parts.note: a seance is a meeting to contact spirits
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A picture of a physician abandoned at a lively gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited' reads as 'lively' but means 'with spirits', a gathering to contact the dead; 'in' puts the doctor and left inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward appearance or likeness.

clue.text: Satisfied with what is inside

explanation.surface: Happy with the contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Content (stressed on the second syllable) means pleased; content (stressed first) means the material contained.

clue.text: Mundane Hartley product

indicators.note: product means something made out of something, so the letters of the name are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: A dull item from someone called Hartley.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartley poses as a manufacturer or a person; it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means worldly, of this world rather than heaven.

clue.text: Competitor in his element ran through

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A contestant at home in their element ran through the course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a race or contest.

clue.text: Root out Liberal not finishing in summer in France

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the French summer

parts.note: ete is French for summer

indicators.note: not finishing means the word for liberal loses its last letter

parts.note: radical means liberal, favouring sweeping reform

explanation.surface: A political liberal who fails to finish is purged during a French summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the last letter of the liberal word, and 'in' puts what is left inside the French summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate something is to destroy it completely, pull it up by the roots.
